title: Differentiability vs continuity
examples: When can a function not be differentiable?
What is the difference between being continuous and differentiable?
How do I check for differentiability at a point?

explain.say: Today we look at when a function is differentiable. First, remember that a function must be continuous to be differentiable. If it is not continuous, it cannot be differentiable.
A corner happens when the graph changes direction sharply. Think about the absolute value function at zero. It has a sharp point there.

items: Example: Absolute value function at zero

draw.text: Corners mean the derivative is undefined.

explain.say: A cusp is a point where the curve comes to a sharp point, but it is different from a corner. The derivative approaches infinity or negative infinity there.
We check one-sided derivatives by approaching the point from only one side. We check the limit from the left and the right separately.
If the left-hand derivative does not equal the right-hand derivative, the function is not differentiable. For example, at x equals zero for the absolute value function.

draw.text: Left derivative must equal right derivative.

faq.q: If a function is continuous, is it always differentiable?
faq.a: No, continuity is only one requirement. The function might still have a corner or a cusp. You must check the slope from both sides.
asks: Must a function be differentiable if it is continuous?
Is continuity enough to guarantee differentiability?

faq.q: What is the main difference between a corner and a cusp?
faq.a: A corner is a sharp point where the slope changes abruptly. A cusp is a point where the slope becomes infinitely steep, either positive or negative.
asks: Are corners and cusps the same thing?
How do I tell if it is a corner or a cusp?

faq.q: How do I calculate the one-sided derivative?
faq.a: You use the limit definition of the derivative, but you only approach the point from one direction. You calculate the limit as x approaches the point from the left, and then from the right.
asks: What is the formula for a one-sided derivative?
Can you show me how to find the left-hand derivative?

faq.q: If the derivative is zero, is the function differentiable?
faq.a: Yes, a derivative of zero simply means the tangent line is horizontal at that point. This is a perfectly differentiable point.
asks: Does a zero derivative mean it is differentiable?
What does a zero derivative tell me about the graph?

faq.q: If a function is not continuous, can it still be differentiable?
faq.a: No. Differentiability implies continuity. If the graph has a break or a jump, the derivative cannot exist at that point.
asks: If it is not continuous, what happens to the derivative?

facts: A function must be continuous at a point to be differentiable there.
At a corner, the left-hand derivative does not equal the right-hand derivative.
A cusp indicates that the derivative approaches positive or negative infinity.
If the left and right derivatives match, the function is differentiable at that point.

options.show: Only if we use the limit definition
options.say: Only if we use the limit definition

quiz.say: If the left-hand derivative equals the right-hand derivative, what does that show?

options.show: The function is differentiable at that point.
options.say: The function is differentiable at that point.

quiz.why: When the one-sided limits of the derivative match, the overall derivative exists.

wrong.0: This is too strong a claim; many curves are differentiable.
wrong.1: This misses the point that matching derivatives prove differentiability.
wrong.2: A cusp implies the derivative approaches infinity, not that the sides match.

quiz.say: Consider a function with a jump discontinuity. What can you conclude about its differentiability?

options.show: It might be differentiable if the jump is small.
options.say: It might be differentiable if the jump is small.

options.show: We must check the one-sided derivatives.
options.say: We must check the one-sided derivatives.

options.show: It is differentiable if the limits exist.
options.say: It is differentiable if the limits exist.

options.show: The function is not differentiable at the point of discontinuity.
options.say: The function is not differentiable at the point of discontinuity.

quiz.why: A break in the graph means the function cannot have a single, well-defined tangent line.

wrong.0: The size of the jump does not change the fact that the function is broken.
wrong.1: Checking one-sided derivatives is pointless if the function is not even defined at the point.
wrong.2: The limits must match and the function must be defined for differentiability.
